question_text: A car moves at a speed of 40 km/h for 15 minutes and then at a speed of 60 km/h for the next 15 minutes. What is the total distance covered by the car? / एक कार 15 मिनट के लिए 40 किमी/घंटा की गति से चलती है और अगले 15 मिनट के लिए 60 किमी/घंटा की गति से चलती है। कार द्वारा तय की गई कुल दूरी कितनी है?
explanation: Distance = Speed × Time. For the first part: Distance = 40 km/h × (15/60) h = 10 km. For the second part: Distance = 60 km/h × (15/60) h = 15 km. Total distance = 10 km + 15 km = 25 km. / दूरी = गति × समय। पहले भाग के लिए: दूरी = 40 किमी/घंटा × (15/60) घंटे = 10 किमी। दूसरे भाग के लिए: दूरी = 60 किमी/घंटा × (15/60) घंटे = 15 किमी। कुल दूरी = 10 किमी + 15 किमी = 25 किमी।
distractor_rationale: Option A (100 km) incorrectly adds speeds directly. Option C (15 km) is only the distance of the second leg. Option D (10 km) is only the distance of the first leg.

ai_context.learning_goal: Apply the speed-distance-time formula for multiple segments of a journey.
common_misconceptions: Students often forget to convert minutes into hours when speed is given in km/h.
ai_context.hint: First, convert 15 minutes into hours by dividing by 60. Then calculate the distance for each part separately.

question_text: Which of the following is an example of oscillatory motion? / निम्नलिखित में से कौन दोलन गति (oscillatory motion) का उदाहरण है?
options: Motion of a car on a straight road / एक सीधी सड़क पर कार की गति
Motion of the Earth around the Sun / सूर्य के चारों ओर पृथ्वी की गति
Motion of a simple pendulum / एक सरल लोलक (pendulum) की गति
Motion of an arrow shot from a bow / धनुष से छोड़े गए तीर की गति
answer: Motion of a simple pendulum / एक सरल लोलक (pendulum) की गति
explanation: Oscillatory or periodic motion is a to-and-fro motion about a fixed mean position. A simple pendulum exhibits this type of motion as it swings back and forth. / दोलन गति वह गति है जो एक निश्चित बिंदु के आगे-पीछे होती है। सरल लोलक इस प्रकार की गति करता है।
distractor_rationale: Option A is linear/rectilinear motion. Option B is circular/periodic but not oscillatory (to-and-fro). Option D is linear/projectile motion.

ai_context.learning_goal: Differentiate oscillatory motion from other types of motion.
common_misconceptions: Students may confuse circular motion with oscillatory motion because both can be periodic.
ai_context.hint: Think about a motion that goes back and forth repeatedly, like a child on a swing.

question_text: What is the basic standard unit (SI unit) of speed? / गति (speed) की मूल मानक इकाई (SI इकाई) क्या है?
explanation: The basic unit of distance is meter (m) and of time is second (s). Therefore, the basic standard unit of speed is meters per second (m/s). / दूरी की मूल इकाई मीटर (m) और समय की सेकंड (s) है। इसलिए, गति की मूल इकाई मीटर/सेकंड (m/s) होती है।
distractor_rationale: Option A, B, and C are valid units of speed used in everyday life, but the international standard (SI) fundamental unit for scientific calculation is m/s.

ai_context.learning_goal: Identify the standard scientific unit (SI) for speed.
common_misconceptions: Students assume km/h is the basic unit because it's seen commonly on vehicle speedometers.
ai_context.hint: What is the most basic scientific unit used for measuring length and the most basic unit for time?

question_text: The distance-time graph for the motion of an object moving with a constant speed is a: / एक समान गति से चलती हुई वस्तु का दूरी-समय ग्राफ कैसा होता है?
explanation: When an object travels equal distances in equal intervals of time, it is in uniform motion. On a distance-time graph, this constant rate of change is represented by a straight line with a constant slope. / जब कोई वस्तु समान समय अंतराल में समान दूरी तय करती है, तो उसे एकसमान गति कहते हैं। दूरी-समय ग्राफ पर यह एक सीधी रेखा से दर्शाया जाता है।
distractor_rationale: Option A happens when speed is changing (acceleration/deceleration). Option C and D do not represent standard physical motion on a time-progressing graph.

ai_context.learning_goal: Interpret distance-time graphs for uniform motion.
common_misconceptions: Students might think uniform motion results in a flat horizontal line (which actually means the object is at rest).
ai_context.hint: If distance increases equally with every tick of the clock, what kind of shape does that plot on a graph?

question_text: If a simple pendulum takes 32 seconds to complete 20 oscillations, what is its time period? / यदि एक सरल लोलक 20 दोलन (oscillations) पूरे करने में 32 सेकंड का समय लेता है, तो उसका आवर्तकाल (time period) क्या होगा?
explanation: Time period is the time taken for ONE complete oscillation. Time Period = Total Time / Number of oscillations = 32 / 20 = 1.6 seconds. / आवर्तकाल एक पूर्ण दोलन का समय है। आवर्तकाल = कुल समय / दोलनों की संख्या = 32 / 20 = 1.6 सेकंड।
distractor_rationale: Option B divides 20 by 32 instead of 32 by 20. Option C is the total time. Option D is the total number of oscillations.

ai_context.learning_goal: Calculate the time period of a simple pendulum given total time and total oscillations.
common_misconceptions: Students often invert the formula and divide oscillations by time, calculating frequency instead of time period.
ai_context.hint: Time period means the time taken for just ONE oscillation. Divide the total time by the number of oscillations.
